paper.title_en: Parity-Dependent Single-Particle Structure in Odd-A Nuclei from a Dunkl Shell Model
paper.abstract_en: Conventional shell-model and mean-field approaches provide a highly successful framework for describing nuclear single-particle spectra. In nuclei with strong octupole correlations or reflection-asymmetric intrinsic shapes, however, effective single-particle spectra may display parity-dependent shifts, parity doublet structures, and parity-dependent average energy shifts that are commonly described through deformation-dependent mean fields, particle-vibration coupling, or beyond-mean-field methods. In this work we explore an effective Dunkl-modified single-particle framework in which the angular part of the kinetic energy is generalized through a Dunkl-type reflection operator. The resulting Hamiltonian contains a control parameter μ that introduces parity-dependent modifications of the effective centrifugal term while recovering the conventional Woods-Saxon limit as the parameter μ tends to zero. The parameter μ is not interpreted as a fundamental deformation variable, but as an effective measure of parity-sensitive correlations within a reduced single-particle description. Calculations are performed for representative nuclei, including near-spherical benchmarks and nuclei known to exhibit octupole correlations. The results show smooth $\mu$-dependent spectral evolution, state-dependent energy shifts, and enhanced sensitivity of low-${\ell}$ orbitals. Moderate reductions of the spectroscopic RMSE are obtained in selected reflection-asymmetric systems, while the conventional limit is recovered for the reflection-symmetric benchmark. The proposed Dunkl Shell Model should therefore be regarded as a phenomenological and symmetry-guided extension of single-particle dynamics, complementary to conventional shell-model, mean-field, and particle-vibration approaches. Its limitations, including the absence of explicit parity projection and collective phonon degrees of freedom, are discussed.
